rfm_tuples.R: Implied management confidence after FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-13) and Q1 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-05-07) into a -47.3% drawdown.
rfm_tuples.f: Parse Form 4 XML for code-P (open-market purchases) by named executives or 10%+ holders across 2025-01-01 to cutoff 2026-05-25. Compare against transaction-code mix and sales volume.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 99 Form 4 filings in the 17 months ending 2026-05-25. 273 non-derivative transactions parsed. Code mix: M=136 (option/RSU exercise), F=116 (withhold-to-cover tax), A=12 (grants), S=7 (sales), J=2 (other), P=0. ZERO open-market purchases by ANY executive, director, or 10%+ holder during the entire window — including the 8-K Apr-6 2026 convertible repayment announcement, the May-7 Q1 print, and the trough of the drawdown. Sales (code S) total $885K: CEO of TheFork (Ambeskovic) 5 sales = $397K, President Brand Tripadvisor (Dalton) 1 sale = $269K, Chief Legal Officer (Kalvert) 1 sale = $218K. Historical baseline check 2023-2024: also 0 code-P purchases (68 Form 4s, 3 sales = $698K) — i.e., absence is consistent management behavior, but it is still notable that none of the C-suite or Chairman Greg Maffei (post-LTRIP merger 2025-04-29 he owns the rolled position directly) bought the dip.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honesty-alpha framing: insiders never buy this stock, so absence by itself isn't acutely informative. However, in a -47.3% drawdown driven by structural SEO/AI-overview deterioration in the cash-cow Hotels segment, the textbook 'management confidence' tape (CEO/CFO/Chairman code-P buy) does NOT appear. Combined with $90M of FY2025 buyback executed at avg $14.72 (now underwater since stock is at the cutoff price implied by -47.3% drawdown) and continued buyback authorization, the company is buying with corporate cash while no executive risks personal capital. Mode-B gap: management says 'foreseeable' liquidity is sufficient but won't put personal $ behind it.

rfm_tuples.R: "We believe that our Hotels and Other segment will continue to be impacted by these challenges and others, including AI overviews displacing top ranked links, reduced click-through rates and a shift towards paid marketing channels." (Q1 2026 10-Q, self-disclosed risk).
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B (implied verification): given the issuer concedes AI-overview displacement, quantify the 2-year arc of Hotels & Other revenue and EBITDA to test how far the cash cow has eroded vs prior peak.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K segment tables + Q1 2026 10-Q segment tables)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Hotels & Other segment (legacy core / cash cow): Revenue 2023 $901.5M → 2024 $818.1M (-9%) → 2025 $750.1M (-8%) → Q1 2026 $186.9M vs $225.7M Q1 2025 = -$38.8M = -17% YoY. Adjusted EBITDA: 2023 $315.2M → 2024 $254.1M (-19%) → 2025 $207.2M (-18%) → Q1 2026 -$24.7M YoY (margin -8.0 pp). EBITDA margin compression: 35.0% → 31.1% → 27.6% → Q1 2026 down 8 pp further. Cumulative segment EBITDA loss from 2023 to 2025 = $108M (-34% of peak). Issuer attributes Q1 2026 hotel meta drop to 'declines in free marketing channels, particularly SEO' with explicit AI-overview disclosure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Hotels segment is in structural, accelerating decline driven by Google AI Overviews compressing SEO click-through. The issuer's own language ('will continue to be impacted') admits this is not cyclical. Q1 2026 -17% revenue acceleration vs FY2025 -8% suggests the Google AI Overviews global rollout in 2024-25 is hitting harder in 2026. This segment historically generated ~60% of consolidated EBITDA — its $108M EBITDA loss over 2 years is the proximate cause of the drawdown. Disclosure is honest, but management's strategic narrative (pivot to Experiences/TheFork) requires those segments to absorb a $300M+ EBITDA hole.

rfm_tuples.R: "The Company is focused on growing and scaling its Experiences marketplace... Importantly, as of the year ended December 31, 2025, the Experiences and TheFork segments represented approximately 60% of the Company's consolidated revenue and 35% of our consolidated adjusted EBITDA."
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: given the strategic pivot claim, quantify whether new-segment EBITDA growth offsets Hotels EBITDA loss on a dollar basis (not just %).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Experiences segment: Revenue 2023 $737.2M → 2024 $840.1M → 2025 $924.4M (+10%); EBITDA $33.3M → $79.1M → $91.1M; margin 4.5% → 9.4% → 9.9%. TheFork: Revenue $153.7M → $180.8M → $220.8M (+22%); EBITDA -$14.5M → $5.3M → $20.4M; margin -9.4% → 2.9% → 9.2%. Sum of 'new' EBITDA growth 2023→2025: ($91.1+$20.4) - ($33.3-$14.5) = $111.5M - $18.8M = +$92.7M. Hotels EBITDA loss 2023→2025: $315.2 → $207.2 = -$108.0M. Net: -$15.3M consolidated EBITDA decline (matches consolidated: $334.0M → $318.7M = -$15.3M, -5%). Q1 2026: Hotels EBITDA -$24.7M YoY while Experiences/TheFork combined Q1 EBITDA improvement is insufficient — consolidated adjusted EBITDA collapsed from +$36.7M Q1'25 to -$19.2M Q1'26, a $55.9M swing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: management's 'pivot is working' narrative is mathematically accurate at the mix-shift level (60% revenue from marketplaces) but masks the dollar reality — Experiences+TheFork EBITDA growth of $93M over 2 years is barely offsetting Hotels EBITDA loss of $108M. In Q1 2026, the pivot stopped working: consolidated EBITDA went from +$36.7M to -$19.2M. The two 'growth' segments cannot grow fast enough in dollars to plug the Hotels hole, which is itself accelerating. The strategic narrative is honest but the math doesn't yet support it as the bull case requires.

rfm_tuples.R: "During 2025, we repurchased 6,105,262 shares of its common stock at an average price of $14.72 per share... or $90 million in the aggregate. As of December 31, 2025, there was $110 million remaining available to repurchase shares."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify FY2025 buyback execution prices vs cutoff-period price (implied -47.3% drawdown from prior peak), and whether management has slowed/accelerated repurchases as price fell.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY2025 repurchases: 6.105M sh at avg $14.72 = $89.9M. Prior year FY2024: 4.725M sh at avg $15.85 = $74.9M. Buyback program $250M authorized Sep-2023 — $110M remains as of Dec-31-2025. Implied price at cutoff given -47.3% drawdown from late-2025 levels would be in low-to-mid single digits. Management bought $90M at $14.72 in 2025; with stock down 47% from that price-area, those buybacks are deeply underwater. No FY2026 buyback figure yet disclosed in Q1 2026 10-Q (need to check share count: basic 125M FY2025 vs 139M FY2024 — the drop reflects buybacks and LTRIP merger collapse of dual-class).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital allocation: management deployed corporate cash at prices materially above current implied cutoff — same pattern seen at many distressed names. Not deception, but a sign management's price-discovery process underestimated SEO/AI-overview structural risk. The $110M remaining authorization combined with $1.0B cash + $345M April 2026 convertible already repaid leaves liquidity intact, but the buyback program isn't a credible value-add at this point.

rfm_tuples.R: "In November 2025, we announced a restructuring plan designed to support the Company's strategic priorities... The plan includes a significant global workforce reduction and other targeted expense reductions." Restructuring charges 2025=$43.4M, 2024=$21.1M, 2023=$22.2M.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify whether restructuring is one-time event or recurring; test management's framing of 'transformation' against multi-year actual charges.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Restructuring & other related reorganization costs: 2023 $22.2M → 2024 $21.1M → 2025 $43.4M (jumped 106% YoY, now 2.3% of revenue vs 1.2% prior). Three consecutive years of restructuring totaling $86.7M — these are recurring transformation costs, not one-time. November 2025 plan announced just two months before the 10-K and explicitly tied to AI-pivot narrative ('positioning as an experiences-led and AI-enabled company'). Multiple 10-K risk factors warn restructuring may impair recruitment ('public nature of the workforce reduction may impair our ability to recruit top talent'), cause attrition ('competitors may target our remaining employees'), and disrupt operations.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Multi-year restructuring at a company with no margin tailwind is a tell — management has been cutting costs for three years and the cash-cow segment still declined 17% in Q1 2026. The Nov-2025 plan is the third round; each appears reactive to deteriorating SEO/AI-overview pressure rather than offensive investment. Honest disclosure of the risks themselves (rare candor about retention risk) — but the recurrence pattern argues this is normalized expense, not transformation.

rfm_tuples.R: "On December 18, 2024, the Company, Liberty TripAdvisor Holdings, Inc. ('LTRIP')... entered into the Merger Agreement... On April 29, 2025, the Merger closed... aggregate transaction price of the Merger was $437 million..." Also: "the Company increased its existing Term Loan B Facility... [$345M] for the redemption of the Company's outstanding 2026 Senior Notes."
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the post-merger capital structure and the increase in debt resulting from collapsing the LTRIP control structure.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K Note 8 Debt + Note on LTRIP merger)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pre-merger: Term Loan B $494M + 0.25% Convertible 2026 Senior Notes $345M = $839M long-term debt at 12/31/2024. Post-merger (12/31/2025): Term Loan B $831M (up $337M from Tack-On Incremental of $341M, March 2025, at SOFR+275bp ≈ 7.1%) plus 2026 Convertible $345M reclassified to current liability for April 2026 maturity. The Convertible 0.25% coupon is being refinanced into a SOFR+275 floating-rate loan = +6.8 pp interest cost on $345M = ~$23M/yr incremental interest expense. Interest expense 2024 $46.4M → 2025 $63.3M (+36%) and will step up further in 2026. Cash $1.0B at 12/31/2025 → $1.03B at 3/31/2026 (Convertible repaid April 1, 2026 from cash). LTRIP merger cost $431M cash plus $6M stock — paid out of cash, reducing buffer. Maffei (LTRIP) remains Chairman. Loan to LTRIP $327M (March 2025) used to retire LTRIP's exchangeable debenture (Certares).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Capital structure became materially worse: trading low-coupon convertible (0.25%) for floating-rate Term Loan B (SOFR+275 ≈ 7%) raises interest expense by ~$23M/yr permanently. The LTRIP merger consumed ~$430M of cash to simplify governance (no controlling stockholder post-merger) — a defensible strategic decision but expensive at $14-15 share price area, especially given the stock fell another 47% from that level. Mode-B observation: management does not emphasize the interest-cost step-up in MD&A — the Q1 2026 interest expense was $15.7M vs $11.7M prior-year (+34%) and rising.

rfm_tuples.R: "Booking (and its subsidiaries) accounted for approximately... 21% and 22% [respectively] of our consolidated revenue." Combined Booking+Expedia ≈25% of consolidated revenue, with 'nearly all' in Hotels and Other segment.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: given the issuer admits ~25% revenue concentration with two CPC-based hotel meta customers in the segment that is in structural AI-overview decline, quantify the dependency risk.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text (10-K customer concentration disclosure + segment data)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Two-customer concentration: Booking+Expedia ≈ 25% of $1,891M consolidated revenue = ~$473M, nearly all in Hotels & Other segment ($750M FY25). Implied: Booking+Expedia ≈ 63% of Hotels & Other segment revenue. Both customers also operate competing hotel-meta and experience marketplaces. The Q1 2026 -17% hotel revenue decline implicitly means Booking/Expedia CPC bids are dropping (they pay TRIP less per click). Multi-year arc: 2023 ~$902M Hotels & Other → 2025 $750M = -$152M (-17%); if Booking/Expedia share held at 63%, their absolute payments to TRIP fell by ~$96M.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode-B catch: the customer concentration disclosure is the standard 10-K boilerplate, but combined with the AI-overview structural decline, TRIP's hotel meta franchise is functionally a two-customer business in terminal decline. Booking and Expedia have both invested heavily in direct supply (Booking owns 1.1M+ hotels via direct contracts; Expedia owns 2M+) — they don't need TRIP's audience as much as they did. The risk of Booking dropping below 10% disclosure threshold (i.e., cutting spend further) is material and the issuer does not quantify the customer-level deterioration.

rfm_tuples.R: "Net income (loss) $(32.4) [Q1 2026] vs $(11.0) [Q1 2025]" — Q1 net loss tripled. Revenue $382.4M vs $398.2M = -4%.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify Q1 2026 acceleration in losses against FY2025 trend; test whether management's 'foreseeable' liquidity claim is robust to continued Hotels EBITDA decline.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025: Revenue $382.4M vs $398.2M (-4%, first quarterly revenue decline in years); Operating loss $(25.2)M vs $(15.5)M (-63% worse); Net loss $(32.4)M vs $(11.0)M (3x worse); Adjusted EBITDA $(19.2)M vs $36.7M ($56M swing). Interest expense $15.7M vs $11.7M (+34%). The deterioration is concentrated in Hotels & Other (EBITDA -$24.7M YoY) plus higher interest from Tack-On Term Loan B. Cash $1.03B at 3/31/26 includes $363M build from Q1 (operating + working capital cycle) before $345M Convertible repayment April 1. Post-repayment cash ≈ $685M plus $496M revolver capacity = $1.18B liquidity. Term Loan B matures July 2031.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The Q1 2026 print is the first window with full-quarter LTRIP merger interest cost AND accelerating SEO/AI-overview damage in hotels. Revenue declining for the first time, EBITDA flipped negative, net loss tripled. Management's 'foreseeable working capital sufficient' statement is technically true (cash + revolver = $1.18B post-Convertible repayment, no covenant issues) but the trajectory means consolidated FCF could turn meaningfully negative in 2026 if Hotels EBITDA losses continue at Q1 pace. No going-concern issue, but the bull case for stabilization has been broken by Q1.

rfm_tuples.R: Implied: insider sales should NOT cluster pre-disclosure of bad news.
rfm_tuples.f: Cross-reference 7 code-S sales in 17mo window against 8-K filing dates for capital events / earnings releases.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 7 code-S sales 2025-01 through 2026-05: Ambeskovic (CEO TheFork) 5 sales spread Aug-2025 and June-2025 ($397K); Dalton (Pres Brand TripAdvisor) 1 sale ~Feb 2025 ($269K); Kalvert (CLO) 1 sale ($218K). All sales precede the Nov-2025 restructuring announcement by 3-9 months and precede the April-2026 8-K / May-2026 Q1 print by 7-12 months. No clustered selling in the 30-day window before the November 2025 restructuring 8-K, the April 2026 8-K, or the May 2026 Q1 release. Total $885K is trivial vs market cap. Most striking is the absence of any C-suite sale during Q4 2025 / Q1 2026 — i.e., insiders held through the drawdown.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No clustered pre-disclosure selling. The IONQ/YSS pattern (insiders dump before bad news) does NOT appear at TRIP. Insiders held through the entire 47% drawdown. This argues against fraud, intentional misleading, or material non-public-information abuse. Honesty-alpha framing: this is a real disclosure-honest distressed name, not a 'liar' candidate.

rfm_tuples.R: "Our management... concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective" as of 12/31/2025.
rfm_tuples.f: Verify ICFR conclusion + auditor opinion + look for material weakness disclosures.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Management concluded ICFR is effective as of 12/31/2025. Auditor PricewaterhouseCoopers (long-tenured) issued unqualified opinion on financial statements and on ICFR. No material weakness disclosed. No CORRESP from SEC indicating issues (16 UPLOAD filings are routine SEC correspondence, not enforcement). No 8-K Item 4.02 (non-reliance) ever filed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Clean controls and clean auditor opinion. No accounting red flags. Combined with no insider selling, this puts TRIP firmly in the 'honest disclosure of bad facts' bucket — i.e., the framework's 'distressed but not lying' archetype (like SRPT 0.125 composite). The framework's contribution should be EXCLUSION of liars, not re-detection of honestly disclosed deterioration.

form4_summary.verdict: Absence of management open-market buying despite -47.3% drawdown; no clustered pre-disclosure selling either; insiders held through the drawdown.

segment_trajectory.narrative: Hotels & Other in structural AI-overview decline; new segments growing but EBITDA dollar growth ($93M over 2yrs) does not yet offset Hotels EBITDA loss ($108M over 2yrs).

summary: TripAdvisor exhibits classic honesty-alpha 'distressed but not lying' archetype. Severity counts: 2 PASS, 4 MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY, 4 SEVERE_UNDERDELIVERY, 0 RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. Top findings: (1) Hotels & Other segment in self-acknowledged AI-overview structural decline, Q1 2026 revenue -17% YoY accelerating from FY2025 -8%; (2) Experiences/TheFork EBITDA growth ($93M over 2yrs) does not yet replace Hotels EBITDA loss ($108M); (3) Q1 2026 consolidated adjusted EBITDA flipped negative ($-19.2M vs +$36.7M prior year). Form-4 insider PURCHASES: ZERO code-P in 17 months (99 Form 4s, 273 tx) — but historical baseline 2023-2024 was also zero, so absence is consistent management behavior rather than acute red flag. No clustered pre-disclosure selling; insiders held through the entire drawdown. Clean ICFR and PwC opinion. Verdict: NEUTRAL leaning SHORT-tier. The fundamental deterioration is real and accelerating, but the disclosure is honest — this is a 'broken business not a fraud' setup. The framework's honesty-alpha contribution here is moderate (TRIP is not a 'liar' to exclude), and the structural AI-overview thesis suggests further downside risk to Hotels segment EBITDA in 2026-2027 before Experiences pivot can mathematically cover the hole.
